intro.heading: The matchup
intro.body:
Thursday night is about first place. **Klein Cain (4–1, 2–1)** walks into Klein Memorial Stadium to face an unbeaten **Klein (6–0, 4–0)** team that just hung **52–0** on Klein Forest. The Bearkats sit tied with Klein Collins atop **District 15-6A**. A Cain win pulls the Hurricanes within a game of the lead; a Klein win gives the Bearkats sole possession of first.

The Hurricanes are coming off their roughest half of the season. Last week's **40–24** loss to Collins saw a **24–14** halftime lead dissolve into a **26–0** second half, with two interceptions and no points after the break. The response starts with the run game. **Eyan Johnson (#16)** managed just 19 yards on nine carries against Collins. Cain needs him back in the middle of things Thursday night.

Dave Campbell's computer likes Klein **by 5** at home. The voters weighed in Monday, too: Dave Campbell's Oct 5 Class 6A poll has Klein at **No. 25 (6-0)**, while the Hurricanes, **No. 25** in the Sep 28 poll, fell out after the Collins loss. VYPE's Houston-area 6A poll, released **Oct 4**, has three Klein ISD schools ranked: **Klein Collins** at **No. 14**, **Klein** at **No. 18**, and **Klein Cain** at **No. 25**. *An unbeaten team favored by less than a touchdown on its own field? We'll see about that Thursday night.*

The playoff math is friendly. Four teams get in from District 15-6A, and Cain sits third at **2–1** with the head-to-head over Tomball in its pocket. And since Cain's 3,784 students make it the district's largest school, a postseason run goes through **Division I**.

players.name: Eyan Johnson
players.copy: Johnson managed just 19 yards on nine carries against Collins, his quietest night of the season. The bounce-back spot is obvious: he still leads Cain at 100.4 rushing yards per game with nine total touchdowns, and his 80-yard kickoff return for a score last week was the highlight of the loss. When he gets going early, everything else opens up.

players.name: Jace Hanks
players.copy: Hanks has thrown eight touchdown passes and run for five more, averaging 85.4 rushing yards a game. But the Collins loss turned on his two second-half interceptions; Cain needs a cleaner game from him Thursday. His legs remain Cain's best broken-play weapon; Klein has to account for him on every snap.

players.name: Cooper Karns
players.copy: Karns leads the Hurricanes at 83.4 receiving yards per game and has been Hanks' most reliable target all season, including six catches for 85 yards against Collins. If Klein loads the box to stop Johnson, the outside throws to Karns become the release valve.

players.name: Jaemin Gilstrap
players.copy: Gilstrap lived in Collins' backfield last week with four tackles and two for loss. He was the Collins offense's biggest problem off the edge. Against a Klein offense that wants to stay on schedule, his edge pressure is the most disruptive force the Hurricanes have.

players.name: Carter Lattelle
players.copy: Lattelle is the engine of the 6–0 start with 12 touchdown passes, spreading the ball to a deep receiver group. He threw for 126 yards and two scores in the early win over Eisenhower and has kept the Bearkats on schedule all season. Pressure him and the whole offense tightens up.

players.name: Mike Brown
players.copy: Brown is Lattelle's first read and the district's most dangerous receiver at 98.2 yards per game with six touchdowns. His 75-yard catch against Eisenhower showed the home-run speed. Cain's corners have to know where he is on every snap.

players.name: Kendrick Brown
players.copy: Kendrick Brown leads a three-headed Klein ground game at 66.2 yards a contest, with Evan Juniel (39.5) and Bryne Johnson (39.3) rotating behind him. The Bearkats stay ahead of the chains running downhill; fitting the run is job one for Cain's front seven.
players.photoCredit: txhsfb (Tony Blalock), via @KleinFootball25 repost; Klein vs Magnolia, Sep 26 2026

players.name: C'Ivion Hines
players.copy: Hines, who goes by "Cash," is the highest-ranked recruit on either roster: 247Sports slots the 2029 linebacker No. 18 overall in the Top247 and No. 2 among linebackers nationally. The 6-foot-3 sophomore already holds a Texas offer and has the Longhorns in his top three. His production matches the pedigree: 41 tackles (6.8 per game, fifth in 15-6A) and an interception for the 6-0 Bearkats. Cain's offense has to know where No. 5 is on every snap.

players.name: Trenton Marshall
players.copy: Marshall is the only player on either roster with a college commitment, pledging to Army on August 17. The 6-foot-1, 280-pound senior plays both lines for the Bearkats. For a Cain front that wants to control the line of scrimmage, moving an Army-bound senior all night is the first problem to solve.

recruiting.heading: Klein recruiting notes
recruiting.note: A roster-wide check of the 2026-27 MaxPreps varsity list, On3's Klein roster page, and 247Sports found one verified college commitment on the current Bearkats roster as of Oct. 8: senior DL Trenton Marshall (Army, 8/17/2026). Reported offers are not commitments. The uncommitted exception is 2029 linebacker C'Ivion Hines, a 247Sports Top247 prospect detailed below.

rows.name: C'Ivion Hines
rows.note: 247Sports ranks the 2029 Klein linebacker No. 2 at his position and No. 18 overall in the Top247. He holds a Texas offer with the Longhorns in his top three among 13 reported offers; uncommitted.

rows.name: Mike Brown
rows.note: The 2028 Klein receiver is unrated by the services but holds reported offers from SMU, Ole Miss, Arizona, Missouri State, and UNLV; On3's prediction machine favors SMU at 81%.

rows.name: Trenton Marshall
rows.note: The 6-1, 280-pound senior defensive lineman is an Army commit (August 17, 2026), the only commitment on either roster.

items.title: Protect the football
items.body: The Collins loss turned on two second-half interceptions, and Klein's secondary takes it away: **Cash Hines (#5)**, **Dyshon Washington (#26)** and **Ashton Vasser (#24)** each have a pick. Give this offense extra possessions and it scores; give them away and Thursday gets long.

items.title: Get Eyan Johnson going early
items.body: Nineteen yards on nine carries was Johnson's quietest night of the year, and the offense stalled with him. Establish the run and **Jace Hanks (#9)** gets the play-action looks that produced **eight** touchdown passes. Cain needs the run game to look like itself again.

items.title: Make someone besides Mike Brown beat you
items.body: **Carter Lattelle (#12)** looks Brown's way first for a reason: **98.2** yards a game and **six** touchdowns. Cloud the coverage his way, tackle the catch, and force the other Bearkat receivers to win one-on-one.

items.title: Fit the run
items.body: Klein rotates three backs averaging over **40** yards a game behind a line opening holes for a **6–0** team. **Jaemin Gilstrap (#42)** set the edge against Collins; the whole front seven has to do it again or the Bearkats will shorten this game.

final.headline: Klein stays perfect, pulls away from Cain 37-14
final.byline: Cain Game Day desk · Updated 10:15 PM CT
final.body:
The first half was a fight. The second half was a lesson.

**Klein (7-0, 5-0)** stayed unbeaten Thursday night at Klein Memorial Stadium, beating **Klein Cain (4-2, 2-2) 37-14** to take sole possession of first place in **District 15-6A**. The Hurricanes led 7-6 after the first quarter and trailed just 15-7 at halftime. Then Klein scored 22 straight.

Cain had its moments early. After Klein punched in the opening touchdown, a **Jace Hanks (#9)** 35-yard keeper and the extra point put Cain up **7-6** with 4:23 left in the first. When Klein marched right back to the Cain 1, the Hurricane defense stuffed fourth-and-goal at the *inch line* to protect the lead. *That was the high-water mark.*

The backbreaker came with 2:25 left in the half. Down 9-7 after a Klein field goal, Cain saw the margin jump to **15-7** when Klein hit **Mike Brown (#1)** for an 86-yard touchdown, the Bearkat junior's biggest play on a night he finished with an estimated five catches for 127 yards. **Gage Hansberger (#34)** blew up the two-point try to keep it a one-score game. Cain answered with a drive to the Klein 24, but Hanks was picked off by **D. Thompson**, and Cain's 39-yard field goal attempt sailed wide left as the half expired.

Klein took control in the third. **Brian Johnson (#4)** finished a long march with a touchdown run to make it **22-7**. Cain recovered the ensuing onside kick and drove to the Klein 5, but turned it over on downs. The Bearkats answered with another touchdown and a two-point conversion to stretch it to **30-7**.

Johnson's 32-yard touchdown run in the fourth pushed it to **37-7** before **Trey Reyes** found **Tyson Freeman (#17)** for a 25-yard score with 57 seconds left to close it out.

The ground game told the story. Klein's rotation of Johnson, **Cortez (#23)** and **Kendrick Brown (#0)** wore the Cain front down, and the Bearkat line owned the second half, a far cry from the goal-line stand that defined Cain's early resistance. Hanks had his moments, including the 35-yard touchdown run and a 53-yard completion to **Earl Oguinn Jr. (#1)**, but two interceptions and the empty red-zone trip kept Cain from keeping pace. **Eyan Johnson (#16)** never found room against a Klein front keyed on him all night.

**Mike Brown (#1)** is the overall Player of the Game, the Klein junior torching Cain for an estimated 127 yards and a touchdown on five catches, including the 86-yard backbreaker. **Gage Hansberger (#34)** is Cain's Player of the Game, the senior linebacker in on stops all night and the man who blew up Klein's two-point try.

Cain drops to **4-2** and **2-2** in district, now two back in the loss column behind unbeaten Klein with four to play. The Hurricanes host Klein Oak next Friday needing a win to stay in the thick of the playoff race.

notes.heading: The inch-line stand
paragraphs: With Cain clinging to a 7-6 first-quarter lead, Klein drove to the Hurricane 1 and went for it on fourth-and-goal. The Cain front stuffed the try at the inch line, the defense’s best moment of the night and the play that kept the early lead intact.

notes.heading: The 86-yarder broke it open
paragraphs: Leading just 9-7 with 2:25 left in the half, Klein hit Mike Brown (#1) for an 86-yard touchdown that pushed the margin to 15-7. Cain drove to the Klein 24 in response, but an interception and a missed 39-yard field goal as time expired sent the Hurricanes to the locker room chasing two scores.

notes.heading: Klein’s ground game took over
paragraphs: The Bearkats’ rotation of Brian Johnson (#4), Cortez (#23) and Kendrick Brown (#0) wore the Cain front down after halftime. Klein scored on its opening third-quarter drive and never looked back, piling up 22 unanswered points before Cain’s late touchdown.
